    14	hypothesis on the package.

   102	    apply GaloisEquivariantOver.ext rho
   103	    exact (w.universal T.left T.hom h.hom h.commutes h.equivariant).choose_spec.1
   104	
   105	/-- The quotient universal-property equivalence commutes with precomposition
   106	in the category of schemes over `Spec K`. -/
   107	theorem overHomEquiv_precomp (w : GaloisQuotientWitness rho Y g)
   108	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)
   109	    (b : T ⟶ Over.mk g) :
   110	    w.overHomEquiv T' (a ≫ b) =
   111	      GaloisEquivariantOver.precomp rho a (w.overHomEquiv T b) := by
   112	  apply GaloisEquivariantOver.ext rho
   113	  change pullbackBaseChange K L g T'.hom (a.left ≫ b.left) _ ≫ w.e.hom =
   114	    pullbackBaseChange K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w ≫
   115	      (pullbackBaseChange K L g T.hom b.left b.w ≫ w.e.hom)
   116	  rw [pullbackBaseChange_comp K L g T.hom T'.hom b.left b.w a.left a.w,
   117	    Category.assoc]
   118	
   119	end GaloisQuotientWitness
   120	
   121	namespace StableAffineOpen
   122	
   123	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
   124	  {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   125	  (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
   126	
   127	/-- Under the orbit-in-an-affine-open hypothesis, the glued invariant-ring
   128	quotient represents equivariant maps after finite Galois base change. -/
   129	noncomputable def gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv
   130	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] [rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen]
   131	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) :
   132	    (T ⟶ gluedQuotientOver rho) ≃ GaloisEquivariantOver rho T :=
   133	  (gluedGaloisQuotientWitness rho).toGaloisQuotientWitness.overHomEquiv T
   134	
   135	/-- The glued-quotient equivalence is natural under precomposition. -/
   136	theorem gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv_precomp
   137	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] [rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen]
   138	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)
   139	    (b : T ⟶ gluedQuotientOver rho) :
   140	    gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv rho T' (a ≫ b) =
   141	      GaloisEquivariantOver.precomp rho a (gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv rho T b) :=
   142	  GaloisQuotientWitness.overHomEquiv_precomp
   143	    (gluedGaloisQuotientWitness rho).toGaloisQuotientWitness a b
   144	
   145	end StableAffineOpen

     1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Pullbacks
     7	import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Galois.Basic
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Semilinear actions on schemes
    11	
    12	This is the scheme-level action vocabulary used by finite-Galois descent.  It
    13	matches the API of the quotient engine in the sibling Algebraic Jacobian
    14	project so that engine can be ported without a parallel set of conventions.
    15	
    16	The inversion in `toSpecAut` is forced by contravariance of `Spec` and by the
    17	group law on categorical automorphisms.  `SemilinearGalAction` then records an
    18	action on a scheme whose structural morphism covers this action on the base.
    19	
    20	## Main declarations
    21	
    22	* `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.toSpecAut`: the action induced on a spectrum.
    23	* `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearGalAction`: a semilinear action on
    24	  a scheme over a field extension.
    25	* `SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen`: the exact geometric condition used
    26	  by the scheme quotient construction.
    27	-/
    28	
    29	set_option autoImplicit false
    30	
    31	universe u
    32	
    33	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry
    34	
    35	namespace AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    36	
    37	section SpecAut
    38	
    39	variable (G : Type*) [Group G] (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    40	  [MulSemiringAction G A]
    41	
    42	lemma toRingHom_comp (gamma tau : G) :
    43	    (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma).comp
    44	        (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A tau) =
    45	      MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (gamma * tau) :=
    46	  RingHom.ext fun x => (mul_smul gamma tau x).symm
    47	
    48	lemma toRingHom_one :
    49	    MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (1 : G) = RingHom.id A :=
    50	  RingHom.ext fun x => one_smul G x
    51	
    52	/-- A group acting on a commutative ring acts on its spectrum.  The inverse in
    53	the ring action makes this a group homomorphism after contravariance of `Spec`.
    54	-/
    55	noncomputable def toSpecAut : G →* Aut (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) :=
    56	  MonoidHom.mk'
    57	    (fun gamma =>
    58	      { hom := Spec.map
    59	          (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma⁻¹))
    60	        inv := Spec.map
    61	          (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma))
    62	        hom_inv_id := by
    63	          rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
    64	            inv_mul_cancel, toRingHom_one, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]
    65	        inv_hom_id := by
    66	          rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
    67	            mul_inv_cancel, toRingHom_one, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id] })
    68	    (fun gamma tau => by
    69	      refine Iso.ext ?_
    70	      change Spec.map
    71	          (CommRingCat.ofHom
    72	            (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (gamma * tau)⁻¹)) =
    73	        Spec.map
    74	            (CommRingCat.ofHom
    75	              (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A tau⁻¹)) ≫
    76	          Spec.map
    77	            (CommRingCat.ofHom
    78	              (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma⁻¹))
    79	      rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
    80	        ← mul_inv_rev])
    81	
    82	lemma toSpecAut_hom (gamma : G) :
    83	    (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom =
    84	      Spec.map
    85	        (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma⁻¹)) :=
    86	  rfl
    87	
    88	lemma toSpecAut_mul_hom (gamma tau : G) :
    89	    (toSpecAut G A (gamma * tau)).hom =
    90	      (toSpecAut G A tau).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom := by
    91	  rw [map_mul]
    92	  rfl
    93	
    94	lemma toSpecAut_inv_hom (gamma : G) :
    95	    (toSpecAut G A gamma⁻¹).hom = (toSpecAut G A gamma).inv := by
    96	  rw [map_inv]
    97	  rfl
    98	
    99	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   100	lemma toSpecAut_hom_inv_hom (gamma : G) :
   101	    (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A gamma⁻¹).hom = 𝟙 _ := by
   102	  rw [toSpecAut_inv_hom, Iso.hom_inv_id]
   103	
   104	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   105	lemma toSpecAut_inv_hom_hom (gamma : G) :
   106	    (toSpecAut G A gamma⁻¹).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom = 𝟙 _ := by
   107	  rw [toSpecAut_inv_hom, Iso.inv_hom_id]
   108	
   109	end SpecAut
   110	
   111	variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
   112	
   113	/-- A semilinear action of the `K`-algebra automorphisms of `L` on an
   114	`L`-scheme.  Each automorphism of the total space covers the corresponding
   115	automorphism of `Spec L`. -/
   116	structure SemilinearGalAction (X : Scheme.{u})
   117	    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) where
   118	  act : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) →* Aut X
   119	  compat (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
   120	    (act gamma).hom ≫ f =
   121	      f ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L gamma).hom
   122	
   123	namespace SemilinearGalAction
   124	
   125	variable {K L} {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   126	
   127	/-- Equivariance of a morphism between semilinearly acted schemes. -/
   128	def IsEquivariant {X' : Scheme.{u}}
   129	    {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   130	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
   131	    (rho' : SemilinearGalAction K L X' f') (h : X ⟶ X') : Prop :=
   132	  ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L,
   133	    (rho.act gamma).hom ≫ h = h ≫ (rho'.act gamma).hom
   134	
   135	/-- The orbit of a point under a semilinear action. -/
   136	def orbit (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (x : X) : Set X :=
   137	  Set.range fun gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (rho.act gamma).hom.base x
   138	
   139	/-- The geometric condition required for the finite-Galois quotient to remain
   140	a scheme: every orbit lies in one affine open. -/
   141	class OrbitsInAffineOpen (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
   142	  exists_affineOpen (x : X) :
   143	    ∃ U : X.affineOpens,
   144	      ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (rho.act gamma).hom.base x ∈ U.1
   145	
   146	/-- A stable open subset of a semilinearly acted scheme. -/
   147	def IsStableOpen (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (U : X.Opens) : Prop :=
   148	  ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (rho.act gamma).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U = U
   149	
   150	end SemilinearGalAction
   151	
   152	/-- A stable affine neighbourhood of every point.  The quotient engine derives
   153	this from `OrbitsInAffineOpen` for finite Galois extensions. -/
   154	class HasStableAffineCover {X : Scheme.{u}}
   155	    {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   156	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
   157	  exists_stable_affineOpen (x : X) :
   158	    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ rho.IsStableOpen U
   159	
   160	end AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.SemilinearAction
     7	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Affine
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Finite subsets in affine opens
    11	
    12	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` is the action-free geometric condition behind the
    13	finite-Galois quotient construction: every finite subset of `X` lies in one
    14	affine open.  For a finite Galois extension, this immediately supplies
    15	`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` for every action on `X`.
    16	
    17	The property is stated independently of Picard data.  In particular, it is a
    18	conclusion to be proved for a representing scheme, not an additional field of
    19	the representability datum.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory
    27	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    30	
    31	/-- Every finite subset of a scheme is contained in a single affine open. -/
    32	def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
    33	  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1
    34	
    35	/-- An affine scheme satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    36	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    37	    FiniteInAffine X :=
    38	  fun _ _ ↦ ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩, fun _ _ ↦ trivial⟩
    39	
    40	/-- `FiniteInAffine` is invariant under isomorphism. -/
    41	theorem finiteInAffine_of_iso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ≅ Y)
    42	    (h : FiniteInAffine X) : FiniteInAffine Y := by
    43	  intro s hs
    44	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (e.hom.base ⁻¹' s)
    45	    (hs.preimage (TopCat.homeoOfIso ((Scheme.forgetToTop).mapIso e)).injective.injOn)
    46	  refine ⟨⟨e.hom ''ᵁ U.1, U.2.image_of_isOpenImmersion e.hom⟩, ?_⟩
    47	  intro y hy
    48	  exact ⟨e.inv.base y, hU (by simpa using hy), by simp⟩
    49	
    50	/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along an affine morphism. -/
    51	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    52	    [IsAffineHom f] (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    53	  intro s hs
    54	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)
    55	  exact ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1, U.2.preimage f⟩, fun x hx ↦ hU ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩⟩
    56	
    57	/-- An object affine over a field spectrum satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    58	theorem finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom {k : Type u} [Field k]
    59	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsAffineHom X.hom] :
    60	    FiniteInAffine X.left :=
    61	  haveI := isAffine_of_isAffineHom X.hom
    62	  finiteInAffine_of_isAffine _
    63	
    64	/-- `FiniteInAffine` supplies the orbit condition for every finite-Galois
    65	semilinear action on the scheme. -/
    66	theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
    67	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    68	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    69	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    70	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (h : FiniteInAffine X) :
    71	    rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen where
    72	  exists_affineOpen x := by
    73	    obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
    74	      h (Set.range fun gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L ↦ (rho.act gamma).hom.base x)
    75	        (Set.finite_range _)
    76	    exact ⟨U, fun gamma ↦ hU ⟨gamma, rfl⟩⟩
    77	
    78	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

   270	      (pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv.app (Opposite.op J)

   272	  Equiv.apply_symm_apply _ _

   275	theorem pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul (gamma tau : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
   276	    pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (gamma * tau) =
   277	      (pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app J ≫
   278	        (pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).map
   279	          (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep tau) ≫

   282	  rw [pic0Galois_homEquiv_twistMor, rep.homEquiv_comp,

   286	      (((pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).op ⋙
   287	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).map
   288	          (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep tau).op

   299	    pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (1 : L ≃ₐ[k] L) =

   318	        (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma).left := by

   320	    (pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul C rep gamma tau)

   327	        ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma).left : J.left ⟶ J.left)) := h

   338	      J.hom ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[k] L) L gamma).hom :=

   346	    have hfixed : @Eq (J.left ⟶ J.left)
   347	        ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (gamma⁻¹ * gamma)).left :
   348	          J.left ⟶ J.left)
   349	        (((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma).left : J.left ⟶ J.left) ≫
   350	          ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma⁻¹).left : J.left ⟶ J.left)) :=

   358	          J.left ⟶ J.left)
   359	        (((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma⁻¹).left : J.left ⟶ J.left) ≫
   360	          ((pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma).left : J.left ⟶ J.left)) :=
   361	      pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul_left C rep gamma gamma⁻¹
   362	    exact hfixed.symm.trans (by
   363	      rw [mul_inv_cancel gamma]
   364	      exact pic0GaloisTwistMor_one_left C rep)

   367	-/
   368	noncomputable def pic0GaloisTwistAction :
   369	    (L ≃ₐ[k] L) →* Aut J.left :=
   370	  MonoidHom.mk' (pic0GaloisTwistAut C rep) fun gamma tau => by
   371	    apply Aut.ext
   372	    exact pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul_left C rep gamma tau

   375	semilinear action required by finite-Galois quotient descent.  No finiteness,
   376	Galois, affine, or additional curve hypothesis is introduced. -/
   377	noncomputable def pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy :
   378	    SemilinearGalAction k L J.left J.hom where
   379	  act := pic0GaloisTwistAction C rep
   380	  compat gamma := pic0GaloisTwistMor_compat C rep gamma

1	/-

     6	import Mathlib
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StableAffineCover
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.GrpObjFoldSum
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# The `G`-stable affine cover for a bare finite group action
    12	
    13	`Sym^n C` is a quotient of `C^n` by `S_n`, and the route to it that
    14	`Albanese/SymPowColimit.lean` §6 identifies — explicit `Scheme.GlueData` from affine charts —
    15	needs one geometric input above all others: **every point has an affine open neighbourhood
    16	stable under the whole group**. Without it the charts cannot be chosen compatibly and the
    17	quotient exists only as an algebraic space (the Hironaka trap recorded in
    18	`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
    19	
    20	That input was believed missing for `S_n`. It is not: `Picard/StableAffineCover.lean` proves
    21	it, sorry-free, and its proof **never uses the Galois structure it is stated over**.
    22	
    23	## What was actually going on
    24	
    25	`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean`'s `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbitsInAffineOpen` is stated
    26	for a `SemilinearGalAction K L X f` — a group homomorphism `Gal(L/K) →* Aut X` *together with*
    27	a field `compat`, the commuting square over `Spec γ` that makes the action semilinear. Reading
    28	the proof, the only things it consumes are `ρ.act` and the two one-line consequences
    29	`act_one_hom` / `act_mul_hom`, which are `map_one` and `map_mul` of the underlying
    30	`MonoidHom`. `compat` — all of the semilinearity — is never mentioned, and
    31	`[FiniteDimensional K L]` is spent only on getting a `Fintype` for `Finset.univ`.
    32	
    33	So the theorem is about a **finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms**; the Galois
    34	data decorates the statement. This file states that version. It is a re-derivation, not a
    35	generalisation of the original in place: `Picard/` belongs to another lane, so the proof is
    36	copied here with the binder replaced (`G →* Aut X` plus `Fintype G`) rather than the original
    37	being weakened. The two files should eventually be one, and the note below says which
    38	direction that should go.
    39	
    40	## Main results
    41	
    42	* `StableGroupAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` — the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis, for a bare action:
    43	  every orbit lies in an affine open. Essential, not technical — see the Hironaka trap.
    44	* `StableGroupAction.IsStableOpen` — a `G`-stable open.
    45	* `exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits` — **the theorem**: under that hypothesis every point
    46	  has a `G`-stable affine open neighbourhood. Prime avoidance puts the orbit in a basic open
    47	  `D(s)` inside `⋂_g g⁻¹U`, and the norm `N = ∏_g g(s)` cuts out a stable affine basic open.
    48	* `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm` — **the `S_n` instantiation**: for `C` a `k̄`-scheme, every
    49	  point of `C^n` has an `S_n`-stable affine open neighbourhood, given the orbit hypothesis.
    50	
    51	**Correction (2026-07-29): the `S_n` producer exists and this file's scope note said it did
    52	not.** Two earlier revisions ran in opposite directions and both were wrong. One advertised a
    53	`permAction : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) →* Aut (C^n)` that did not exist; the correction then
    54	recorded building it as blocked, on the grounds that `MonObj.permAut` "is a bare morphism
    55	never shown to be an isomorphism" and `SymPowColimit.permEnd` "lands in `End`, not `Aut`".
    56	Both grounds were accurate statements about the tree and the inference from them was not:
    57	`permAut C σ⁻¹` is a two-sided inverse of `permAut C σ`, because
    58	`permAut C σ ≫ permAut C τ = permAut C (σ * τ)`. That is `MonObj.permAut_comp`, and the
    59	action is `MonObj.permAutHom`, both now in `Albanese/GrpObjFoldSum.lean` — four lines, no
    60	construction. The lesson is the `permEnd` convention: the inverse `permEnd` carries is forced
    61	by `End`'s reversed multiplication, and reading it as a fact about `permAut` is what made an
    62	isomorphism look absent.
    63	
    64	## Why the proof needs no averaging, and so no characteristic hypothesis
    65	
    66	The norm `∏_g g(s)` is a *product*, not an average: it needs no `1/|G|` and works in every
    67	characteristic. That matters here for the same reason it matters in
    68	`Albanese/SymPowTensorAction.lean` — `g!` may vanish in `k̄` when `char k̄ ≤ g`, so any route
    69	through averaging would exclude exactly the cases the challenge is stated over.
    70	
    71	## Scope — what this does and does not give
    72	
    73	**Does**: prove the stable-cover statement at the generality a glue-data construction wants —
    74	a *finite group acting on a scheme by automorphisms*, with no Galois hypothesis and no
    75	characteristic hypothesis.
    76	
    77	**Does** now also apply it to `S_n` acting on `C^n`: `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm` for the
    78	product in `Scheme`, and `exists_stable_affineOpen_perm_over` for the underlying scheme of the
    79	`Over (Spec k̄)`-product — **which is the one the leg uses**, and is a different object (see
    80	that theorem's docstring; `Over.forget` does not preserve binary products).
    81	
    82	**Does not**: build the glue data. `HasColimit (permDiagram C g)` remains open and
    83	`AlbaneseUP.lean`'s six sorries are unchanged.
    84	
    85	**The count, in one place, because three places in this tree disagreed about it.** A glue-data
    86	assembly needs *four* things:
    87

    10	/-!
    11	# Finite subsets of irreducible algebraic groups lie in affine opens
    12	
    13	This file formalizes the irreducible, algebraically closed core of
    14	[Stacks, Lemma 39.8.6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B7S). Translation
    15	turns one affine neighborhood of the identity into finitely many dense open
    16	subsets. Irreducibility gives a common closed point, and translating back gives
    17	one affine open containing the prescribed rational points.
    18	
    19	The final theorem applies this argument to arbitrary finite sets of topological
    20	points: local finite type over a field makes the scheme Jacobson, so each point
    21	specializes to a closed point. It deliberately does not assert the remaining
    22	arbitrary-field or reducible-component descent.
    23	-/

    30	open MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
    31	open scoped CategoryTheory.MonObj
    32	
    33	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme
    34	
    35	variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
    36	
    37	/-- Right translation by a rational point of a group scheme. -/
    38	noncomputable def rightMul (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
    39	    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ⟶ G :=
    40	  lift (𝟙 G) (toUnit G ≫ p) ≫ μ
    41	
    42	lemma comp_rightMul {G Z : Over (Spec (.of K))} [GrpObj G]
    43	    (x : Z ⟶ G) (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) :
    44	    x ≫ rightMul G p = x * (toUnit Z ≫ p) := by
    45	  rw [rightMul, ← Category.assoc, comp_lift, Category.comp_id, comp_toUnit_assoc,
    46	    CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
    47	
    48	/-- Right translation is inverted by translation by the inverse point. -/
    49	noncomputable def rightMulIso (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
    50	    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ≅ G where
    51	  hom := rightMul G p
    52	  inv := rightMul G (p ≫ ι)
    53	  hom_inv_id := by
    54	    rw [comp_rightMul, rightMul, ← CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
    55	    change ((𝟙 G) * (toUnit G ≫ p)) * (toUnit G ≫ p)⁻¹ = 𝟙 G
    56	    simp
    57	  inv_hom_id := by
    58	    rw [comp_rightMul, rightMul, ← CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
    59	    change ((𝟙 G) * (toUnit G ≫ p)⁻¹) * (toUnit G ≫ p) = 𝟙 G
    60	    simp
    61	
    62	/-- Left translation by a rational point of a group scheme. -/
    63	noncomputable def leftMul (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
    64	    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ⟶ G :=
    65	  lift (toUnit G ≫ p) (𝟙 G) ≫ μ
    66	
    67	lemma comp_leftMul {G Z : Over (Spec (.of K))} [GrpObj G]
    68	    (x : Z ⟶ G) (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) :
    69	    x ≫ leftMul G p = (toUnit Z ≫ p) * x := by
    70	  rw [leftMul, ← Category.assoc, comp_lift, Category.comp_id, comp_toUnit_assoc,
    71	    CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
    72	
    73	/-- Left translation is inverted by translation by the inverse point. -/
    74	noncomputable def leftMulIso (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
    75	    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ≅ G where
    76	  hom := leftMul G p
    77	  inv := leftMul G (p ≫ ι)
    78	  hom_inv_id := by
    79	    rw [comp_leftMul, leftMul, ← CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
    80	    change (toUnit G ≫ p)⁻¹ * ((toUnit G ≫ p) * (𝟙 G)) = 𝟙 G
    81	    simp
    82	  inv_hom_id := by
    83	    rw [comp_leftMul, leftMul, ← CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
    84	    change (toUnit G ≫ p) * ((toUnit G ≫ p)⁻¹ * (𝟙 G)) = 𝟙 G
    85	    simp
    86	
    87	lemma point_comp_rightMul_eq_point_comp_leftMul
    88	    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
    89	    (p q : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) :
    90	    p ≫ rightMul G q = q ≫ leftMul G p := by
    91	  rw [comp_rightMul, comp_leftMul]
    92	  simp

    94	/-- Over an algebraically closed field, finitely many rational points of an
    95	irreducible locally algebraic group lie in one affine open. -/
    96	theorem exists_affineOpen_finset_points_of_irreducible
    97	    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G] [IsAlgClosed K]
    98	    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [IrreducibleSpace G.left]
    99	    (s : Finset (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G)) :
   100	    ∃ A : G.left.affineOpens,
   101	      ∀ p ∈ s, p.left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) ∈ A.1 := by
   102	  classical
   103	  let e : G.left := η[G].left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)
   104	  obtain ⟨U, hUa, heU, -⟩ :=
   105	    (TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp G.left.isBasis_affineOpens)
   106	      (show e ∈ (⊤ : G.left.Opens) from trivial)
   107	  let A : G.left.affineOpens := ⟨U, hUa⟩
   108	  let V : (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) → Set G.left :=
   109	    fun p ↦ ((leftMulIso G p).hom.left ⁻¹ᵁ A.1 : Set G.left)
   110	  let F : Finset (Set G.left) := s.image V
   111	  have hVopen (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : IsOpen (V p) :=
   112	    A.1.isOpen.preimage (Scheme.Hom.continuous (leftMulIso G p).hom.left)
   113	  have hVnonempty (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : (V p).Nonempty := by
   114	    let x := (p ≫ ι).left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)
   115	    refine ⟨x, ?_⟩
   116	    change (leftMul G p).left ((p ≫ ι).left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)) ∈ U
   117	    have h : (p ≫ ι) ≫ leftMul G p = η[G] := by
   118	      rw [comp_leftMul]
   119	      change p * p⁻¹ = η[G]
   120	      exact (mul_inv_cancel p).trans (by
   121	        rw [CategoryTheory.Hom.one_def]
   122	        simp)
   123	    rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, ← Over.comp_left, h]
   124	    exact heU
   125	  have hFopen : ∀ W ∈ F, IsOpen W := by
   126	    intro W hW
   127	    obtain ⟨p, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hW
   128	    exact hVopen p
   129	  have hFnonempty : ∀ W ∈ F, W.Nonempty := by
   130	    intro W hW
   131	    obtain ⟨p, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hW
   132	    exact hVnonempty p
   133	  have hIrr := (isIrreducible_iff_sInter.mp
   134	    (IrreducibleSpace.isIrreducible_univ G.left)) F hFopen (by
   135	      intro W hW
   136	      simpa using hFnonempty W hW)
   137	  have hInter : (⋂₀ (↑F : Set (Set G.left))).Nonempty := by
   138	    simpa using hIrr
   139	  have hInterOpen : IsOpen (⋂₀ (↑F : Set (Set G.left))) :=
   140	    F.finite_toSet.isOpen_sInter hFopen
   141	  letI : JacobsonSpace G.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace G.hom
   142	  obtain ⟨g, hgF, hgc⟩ :=
   143	    nonempty_inter_closedPoints hInter hInterOpen.isLocallyClosed
   144	  let q0 := (pointEquivClosedPoint G.hom).symm ⟨g, hgc⟩
   145	  let q : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G := Over.homMk q0.1 q0.2
   146	  have hq : q.left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = g := by
   147	    dsimp [q, q0]
   148	    exact pointOfClosedPoint_apply G.hom g hgc (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)
   149	  refine ⟨⟨(rightMulIso G q).hom.left ⁻¹ᵁ A.1,
   150	    A.2.preimage (rightMulIso G q).hom.left⟩, ?_⟩
   151	  intro p hp
   152	  have hpF : V p ∈ F := Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩
   153	  have hgp : g ∈ V p := Set.mem_sInter.mp hgF _ hpF
   154	  change (rightMul G q).left (p.left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)) ∈ U
   155	  rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, ← Over.comp_left,
   156	    point_comp_rightMul_eq_point_comp_leftMul G p q,
   157	    Over.comp_left, Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, hq]
   158	  exact hgp
   159	
   160	/-- Every finite set of topological points of an irreducible locally algebraic
   161	group over an algebraically closed field lies in one affine open. -/
   162	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAlgClosed_of_irreducible
   163	    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G] [IsAlgClosed K]
   164	    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [IrreducibleSpace G.left] :
   165	    Scheme.FiniteInAffine G.left := by
   166	  classical
   167	  intro s hs
   168	  lift s to Finset G.left using hs with t ht
   169	  letI : JacobsonSpace G.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace G.hom
   170	  have hclosed (x : G.left) :
   171	      ∃ y : G.left, y ∈ closure {x} ∧ y ∈ closedPoints G.left := by
   172	    have hnonempty : (closure ({x} : Set G.left)).Nonempty :=
   173	      ⟨x, subset_closure (Set.mem_singleton x)⟩
   174	    obtain ⟨y, hy, hyc⟩ :=
   175	      nonempty_inter_closedPoints hnonempty isClosed_closure.isLocallyClosed
   176	    exact ⟨y, hy, hyc⟩
   177	  choose y hy using hclosed
   178	  let p0 (x : G.left) := (pointEquivClosedPoint G.hom).symm ⟨y x, (hy x).2⟩
   179	  let p (x : G.left) : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G :=
   180	    Over.homMk (p0 x).1 (p0 x).2
   181	  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ :=
   182	    exists_affineOpen_finset_points_of_irreducible G (t.image p)
   183	  refine ⟨A, ?_⟩
   184	  intro x hx
   185	  have hxt : x ∈ t := by
   186	    exact_mod_cast hx
   187	  have hp : p x ∈ t.image p := Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x, hxt, rfl⟩
   188	  have hpx : (p x).left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = y x := by
   189	    dsimp [p, p0]
   190	    exact pointOfClosedPoint_apply G.hom (y x) (hy x).2
   191	      (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)
   192	  have hpy : y x ∈ A.1 := hpx ▸ hA (p x) hp
   193	  exact (specializes_iff_mem_closure.mpr (hy x).1).mem_open A.1.isOpen hpy
   194	
   195	end AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme

     8	/-!
     9	# Group schemes are separated (Kleiman `lem:agps`(1), Wave-5 X1)
    10	
    11	A group scheme over a field is separated: the diagonal
    12	`Δ : G ⟶ G ⊗ G` is the pullback of the unit section `η[G]` along the *difference map*
    13	`fst ⋅ snd⁻¹ : G ⊗ G ⟶ G` ("`(x, y) ↦ x y⁻¹`"), and the unit section of a group scheme
    14	over a field is a closed immersion (mathlib, `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean`), so
    15	the diagonal is a closed immersion by stability under base change.
    16	
    17	Stated as reusable infrastructure, in three layers:
    18	
    19	* `CategoryTheory.GrpObj.isPullback_diagonal` — the purely categorical half, for a group
    20	  object in ANY cartesian monoidal category: the square
    21	
    22	  ```
    23	        G ------ lift (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G) -----> G ⊗ G
    24	        |                                  |
    25	     toUnit G                       fst G G * (snd G G)⁻¹
    26	        |                                  |
    27	        v                                  v
    28	      𝟙_ C ---------- η[G] -------------> G
    29	  ```
    30	
    31	  is a pullback (the Hom-group calculus of `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian`
    32	  does all the work).
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one` — a group scheme over an
    34	  ARBITRARY base scheme whose unit section is a closed immersion is separated.  Note:
    35	  no finiteness hypothesis whatsoever (`LocallyOfFiniteType` is NOT needed).
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_grpObj` (instance) — over a field the closed-
    37	  immersion hypothesis is mathlib's instance, so every group scheme over a field is
    38	  separated.
    39	
    40	The Wave-5 datum corollary `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.isSeparated` closes the
    41	file: `d.J.hom` is separated for every Jacobian datum `d` — one of the two inputs of
    42	the properness assembly P3 (`IsProper = IsSeparated + UniversallyClosed + lft`).
    43	-/
    44	
    45	set_option autoImplicit false
    46	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    47	
    48	universe v₁ u₁ u
    49	
    50	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
    51	
    52	namespace CategoryTheory
    53	
    54	section Categorical
    55	
    56	variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] [CartesianMonoidalCategory C]
    57	
    58	/-- **The diagonal of a group object is the pullback of the unit along the difference
    59	map** (Kleiman `lem:agps`(1), categorical half): for a group object `G` in a cartesian
    60	monoidal category, the square with top `Δ = lift (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G)`, left `toUnit G`, right
    61	the difference map `fst ⋅ snd⁻¹ : G ⊗ G ⟶ G`, and bottom the unit `η[G]` is a
    62	pullback.  Here `⋅`/`⁻¹` are the Hom-group operations on `G ⊗ G ⟶ G` (scoped in
    63	`CategoryTheory.MonObj`), so the difference map is `lift (fst G G) (snd G G ≫ ι) ≫ μ`
    64	definitionally. -/
    65	theorem GrpObj.isPullback_diagonal (G : C) [GrpObj G] :
    66	    IsPullback (toUnit G) (lift (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G)) η[G] (fst G G * (snd G G)⁻¹) where
    67	  w := by
    68	    rw [MonObj.comp_mul, GrpObj.comp_inv, lift_fst, lift_snd, mul_inv_cancel, Hom.one_def]
    69	  isLimit' := Nonempty.intro <| PullbackCone.IsLimit.mk _
    70	    (fun s => s.snd ≫ fst G G)
    71	    (fun s => toUnit_unique _ _)
    72	    (fun s => by
    73	      -- the cone condition says `(s.snd ≫ fst) ⋅ (s.snd ≫ snd)⁻¹ = 1` in the Hom-group
    74	      have key : s.snd ≫ fst G G = s.snd ≫ snd G G := by
    75	        have h := s.condition.symm
    76	        rw [MonObj.comp_mul, GrpObj.comp_inv, toUnit_unique s.fst (toUnit _),
    77	          ← Hom.one_def] at h
    78	        exact mul_inv_eq_one.mp h
    79	      exact CartesianMonoidalCategory.hom_ext _ _ (by simp) (by simpa using key))
    80	    (fun s m hm₁ hm₂ => by
    81	      have := hm₂ =≫ fst G G
    82	      simpa using this)
    83	
    84	end Categorical
    85	
    86	end CategoryTheory
    87	
    88	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    89	
    90	/-- **A group scheme with closed unit section is separated** (Kleiman `lem:agps`(1)):
    91	for a group object `G` of `Over S`, `S` any base scheme, if the unit section
    92	`η[G].left : S ⟶ G.left` is a closed immersion then `G.hom` is separated.  The
    93	diagonal is the base change of `η[G].left` along the difference map
    94	(`GrpObj.isPullback_diagonal`, pushed to schemes by `Over.forget`), and closed
    95	immersions are stable under base change.  No finiteness hypothesis is needed. -/
    96	theorem isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Over S) [GrpObj G]
    97	    [IsClosedImmersion η[G].left] : IsSeparated G.hom := by
    98	  constructor
    99	  have sq := (GrpObj.isPullback_diagonal G).map (Over.forget S)
   100	  have h : IsClosedImmersion (lift (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G)).left :=
   101	    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sq ‹IsClosedImmersion η[G].left›
   102	  exact h
   103	
   104	/-- **A group scheme over a field is separated** (Kleiman `lem:agps`(1)): the unit
   105	section is a closed immersion by mathlib's group-scheme instance
   106	(`AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean`), and `isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one`
   107	applies.  No `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis is needed. -/
   108	instance isSeparated_of_grpObj {K : Type u} [Field K] (G : Over (Spec (.of K)))
   109	    [GrpObj G] : IsSeparated G.hom :=
   110	  isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one G
   111	
   112	/-- **Wave-5 X1, datum corollary**: the representing object of every Jacobian datum is
   113	separated over `k`.  Feeds the properness assembly P3
   114	(`IsProper = IsSeparated + UniversallyClosed + LocallyOfFiniteType`). -/
   115	theorem JacobianData.isSeparated {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   116	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   117	    (d : JacobianData C) : IsSeparated d.J.hom :=
   118	  letI := d.grpObj
   119	  isSeparated_of_grpObj d.J
   120	
   121	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# Homogeneity of a group scheme: translations, and the invariants they move
    10	
    11	A group scheme is **homogeneous**: any point can be carried to any other by an automorphism
    12	of the underlying scheme, namely a translation. This file supplies the translation and the
    13	consequence the dimension chapter needs — that a *pointwise* invariant of the local rings is
    14	constant along the orbit of the translations, so a bound at one point is a bound at every
    15	point in that orbit.
    16	
    17	## Why this file exists
    18	
    19	`Picard/Pic0Dimension.lean` reduces `dim Pic⁰_{C/k} = g(C)` to two halves. The `≥` half
    20	needs the cotangent dimension at the **identity** only, and is front (a) of this chapter.
    21	The `≤` half is
    22	```
    23	∀ z, dim_{κ(z)} (m_z / m_z²) ≤ g
    24	```
    25	— a bound at *every* point
    26	(`Pic0.topologicalKrullDim_le_genus_of_forall_finrank_cotangentSpace_le`).
    27	The previous reading of that hypothesis was that it is a genuinely new *uniform* statement,
    28	different in kind from the one-point identity front (a) produces. On a **group** scheme that
    29	reading is too pessimistic, and this file records why: translations act transitively on the
    30	rational points, and they are isomorphisms of the underlying scheme, so the cotangent
    31	dimension is the same at any two points connected by one.
    32	
    33	What this does and does not buy, stated precisely because the distinction is the whole
    34	content:
    35	
    36	* it **does** turn the uniform hypothesis into a statement about *one* orbit representative
    37	  plus a transitivity statement about the points — `finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_of_pointTranslation`
    38	  is the transport, and it is unconditional;
    39	* it does **not** by itself discharge the uniform hypothesis, because the translations here are
    40	  indexed by *sections* `𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G`, i.e. by `S`-rational points, and a scheme over a
    41	  non-closed field has points that are not rational. Over an algebraically closed field the
    42	  closed points are all rational and the orbit is the whole closed-point set; in general the
    43	  residue-field extension is the gap. So the honest statement of what remains is "every point
    44	  of `Pic⁰` is a translate of the identity", which is a statement about *points*, not about
    45	  dimension theory.
    46	
    47	That is a strictly better place for the residue than "a uniform cotangent bound", which is
    48	what the roadmap recorded before: it moves the open content out of dimension theory (where
    49	this project had to build `Picard/EmbeddingDimensionBound.lean` to make progress) and into
    50	the homogeneity of a group scheme, where the mathematics is standard.
    51	
    52	## Provenance
    53	
    54	`CategoryTheory.GrpObj.pointTranslation` and its scheme-level shadow are ported from the
    55	sibling project `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`,
    56	`AlgebraicJacobian/AbelianVariety/Translation.lean` (sorry-free there). The port is free:
    57	the general half is pure `CartesianMonoidalCategory` reasoning on top of mathlib's
    58	`CategoryTheory.GrpObj.mulRight` (`M…7812 tokens truncated…nd the `open`s are the same.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange` — the
    45	  criterion this project actually consumes: `G ⟶ Spec k` is smooth as soon as the base change
    46	  `G ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄` is reduced. No `GeometricallyReduced`, no quantifier over fields.
    47	
    48	## Change of attack surface, NOT of strength — corrected after review
    49	
    50	An earlier version of this docstring called the criterion's hypothesis **strictly weaker** than
    51	`smooth_of_grpObj`'s. **That is wrong in this project, and the correction is the interesting
    52	part.** Fresh-context review (run 0067) established:
    53	
    54	* in **mathlib alone**, `IsReduced`-over-`k̄ ⟹ GeometricallyReduced` is indeed unavailable —
    55	  `infer_instance` fails for it on a bare `import Mathlib`;
    56	* but **this project owns the converse**: `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`
    57	  (`AlgebraicJacobian/Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean`, an instance) derives the class from
    58	  smoothness. So `IsReduced`-over-`k̄` → (this criterion) → `Smooth` → `GeometricallyReduced`
    59	  closes by `inferInstance`, axiom-clean.
    60	
    61	At these binders the two hypotheses are therefore **interprovable**, and this file is a
    62	restatement rather than a weakening. The mistake was methodological and worth recording: the
    63	"missing in mathlib" measurement was taken inside the *edited file's* import cone (99 modules),
    64	which does not contain `Curve/GeometricallyReduced`, while the root cone (215 modules) does.

     9	/-!
    10	# The orbit condition collapses the dimension: `htrans → dim = 0`
    11	
    12	`Picard/GroupSchemeHomogeneity.lean` reduces the A.3 dimension statement
    13	`dim Pic⁰_{C/k} = g(C)` to three local inputs, one of which is the **orbit condition**
    14	
    15	```
    16	htrans : ∀ z, ∃ x y : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec k)) ⟶ Pic0Scheme C,
    17	           (pointTranslationIso (Pic0Scheme C) x y).hom.base e = z
    18	```
    19	
    20	("every point of `Pic⁰` is a `k`-rational translate of the identity"), recorded there as "the
    21	honest gap" — a statement about *points* rather than about dimension theory, expected to be
    22	cheap over `k̄` and a descent question in general.
    23	
    24	**That reading is wrong, and this file proves it.** The orbit condition is not a weak
    25	point-counting hypothesis waiting for a descent argument: it is strong enough to force
    26	
    27	```
    28	topologicalKrullDim Pic⁰_{C/k} = 0,
    29	```
    30	
    31	so `topologicalKrullDim_eq_genus_of_homogeneous` and
    32	`isAbelianVariety_of_dimension_genus` are, on their `htrans` hypothesis, only ever
    33	inhabited when `g(C) = 0`. For a genus `≥ 1` curve — the entire point of the A.3 leg,
    34	whose gate `thm:nonempty_jacobianWitness` is stated for `g(C) ≥ 1` — the hypothesis set of
    35	those two theorems is **contradictory**. They are true, and vacuous where it matters.
    36	
    37	## Why (three steps, all proved below)
    38	
    39	1. `pointTranslationIso` is an **isomorphism of schemes**, so its base map is a homeomorphism
    40	   (`Scheme.homeoOfIso`). A homeomorphism carries closed points to closed points.
    41	2. The identity point `e` **is** a closed point: it is the image of the section
    42	   `identitySection : Spec k ⟶ Pic⁰`, and a section of a morphism to `Spec k` is a closed
    43	   immersion (`isClosedImmersion_of_comp_eq_id`, using `Subsingleton (Spec k)`), whose range is
    44	   that single point. So `htrans` says every point of `Pic⁰` is a homeomorphic image of a
    45	   *closed* point, i.e. every singleton is closed: `Pic⁰` is `T1`.
    46	3. A scheme is sober, and in a **sober `T1`** space the irreducible closeds are
    47	   order-isomorphic to the points under the specialization order
    48	   (`irreducibleSetEquivPoints`), which `T1` makes trivial (`Specializes.eq`). A poset with no
    49	   strict `<` has `krullDim = 0`. Hence `topologicalKrullDim = 0`.
    50	
    51	Step 3 is the reusable half: `topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero_of_t1Space` below holds for any
    52	nonempty sober `T1` space and is stated separately for that reason.
    53	
    54	## What this does and does not say
    55	
    56	It does **not** refute `dim Pic⁰ = g`, which is true. It refutes the *reduction*: passing
    57	through a `k`-rational orbit condition cannot reach it, because `k`-rational translations only
    58	ever move closed points to closed points while `Pic⁰` of a positive-genus curve has
    59	non-closed points (its generic point). The mathematics that reduction was standing in for —
    60	the `≤` half's uniform cotangent bound — therefore still needs a route that reaches
    61	**non-closed** points: transport along a translation by a point valued in an extension of
    62	`k`, or a generic-point argument, not an orbit of `k`-sections.
    63	
    64	The rest of `GroupSchemeHomogeneity.lean` is unaffected: the cotangent-invariance theorems
    65	(`finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_of_ringEquiv`, `finrank_cotangentSpace_stalk_eq_of_isIso`) are
    66	about a single isomorphism and are exactly as useful as before. What is refuted is the *shape*
    67	of the hypothesis those theorems were assembled behind.
    68	-/

+import AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.FiniteInAffine
+import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Group.Smooth
+import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Grp
+
+/-!
+# Finite subsets of irreducible algebraic groups lie in affine opens
+
+This file formalizes the irreducible, algebraically closed core of
+[Stacks, Lemma 39.8.6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B7S). Translation
+turns one affine neighborhood of the identity into finitely many dense open
+subsets. Irreducibility gives a common closed point, and translating back gives
+one affine open containing the prescribed rational points.
+
+The final theorem applies this argument to arbitrary finite sets of topological
+points: local finite type over a field makes the scheme Jacobson, so each point
+specializes to a closed point. It deliberately does not assert the remaining
+arbitrary-field or reducible-component descent.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+universe u
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits
+open MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
+open scoped CategoryTheory.MonObj
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme
+
+variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
+
+/-- Right translation by a rational point of a group scheme. -/
+noncomputable def rightMul (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
+    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ⟶ G :=
+  lift (𝟙 G) (toUnit G ≫ p) ≫ μ
+
+lemma comp_rightMul {G Z : Over (Spec (.of K))} [GrpObj G]
+    (x : Z ⟶ G) (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) :
+    x ≫ rightMul G p = x * (toUnit Z ≫ p) := by
+  rw [rightMul, ← Category.assoc, comp_lift, Category.comp_id, comp_toUnit_assoc,
+    CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
+
+/-- Right translation is inverted by translation by the inverse point. -/
+noncomputable def rightMulIso (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
+    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ≅ G where
+  hom := rightMul G p
+  inv := rightMul G (p ≫ ι)
+  hom_inv_id := by
+    rw [comp_rightMul, rightMul, ← CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
+    change ((𝟙 G) * (toUnit G ≫ p)) * (toUnit G ≫ p)⁻¹ = 𝟙 G
+    simp
+  inv_hom_id := by
+    rw [comp_rightMul, rightMul, ← CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
+    change ((𝟙 G) * (toUnit G ≫ p)⁻¹) * (toUnit G ≫ p) = 𝟙 G
+    simp
+
+/-- Left translation by a rational point of a group scheme. -/
+noncomputable def leftMul (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
+    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ⟶ G :=
+  lift (toUnit G ≫ p) (𝟙 G) ≫ μ
+
+lemma comp_leftMul {G Z : Over (Spec (.of K))} [GrpObj G]
+    (x : Z ⟶ G) (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) :
+    x ≫ leftMul G p = (toUnit Z ≫ p) * x := by
+  rw [leftMul, ← Category.assoc, comp_lift, Category.comp_id, comp_toUnit_assoc,
+    CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
+
+/-- Left translation is inverted by translation by the inverse point. -/
+noncomputable def leftMulIso (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
+    (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : G ≅ G where
+  hom := leftMul G p
+  inv := leftMul G (p ≫ ι)
+  hom_inv_id := by
+    rw [comp_leftMul, leftMul, ← CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
+    change (toUnit G ≫ p)⁻¹ * ((toUnit G ≫ p) * (𝟙 G)) = 𝟙 G
+    simp
+  inv_hom_id := by
+    rw [comp_leftMul, leftMul, ← CategoryTheory.Hom.mul_def]
+    change (toUnit G ≫ p) * ((toUnit G ≫ p)⁻¹ * (𝟙 G)) = 𝟙 G
+    simp
+
+lemma point_comp_rightMul_eq_point_comp_leftMul
+    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
+    (p q : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) :
+    p ≫ rightMul G q = q ≫ leftMul G p := by
+  rw [comp_rightMul, comp_leftMul]
+  simp
+
+/-- Over an algebraically closed field, finitely many rational points of an
+irreducible locally algebraic group lie in one affine open. -/
+theorem exists_affineOpen_finset_points_of_irreducible
+    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G] [IsAlgClosed K]
+    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [IrreducibleSpace G.left]
+    (s : Finset (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G)) :
+    ∃ A : G.left.affineOpens,
+      ∀ p ∈ s, p.left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) ∈ A.1 := by
+  classical
+  let e : G.left := η[G].left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)
+  obtain ⟨U, hUa, heU, -⟩ :=
+    (TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp G.left.isBasis_affineOpens)
+      (show e ∈ (⊤ : G.left.Opens) from trivial)
+  let A : G.left.affineOpens := ⟨U, hUa⟩
+  let V : (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) → Set G.left :=
+    fun p ↦ ((leftMulIso G p).hom.left ⁻¹ᵁ A.1 : Set G.left)
+  let F : Finset (Set G.left) := s.image V
+  have hVopen (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : IsOpen (V p) :=
+    A.1.isOpen.preimage (Scheme.Hom.continuous (leftMulIso G p).hom.left)
+  have hVnonempty (p : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G) : (V p).Nonempty := by
+    let x := (p ≫ ι).left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)
+    refine ⟨x, ?_⟩
+    change (leftMul G p).left ((p ≫ ι).left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)) ∈ U
+    have h : (p ≫ ι) ≫ leftMul G p = η[G] := by
+      rw [comp_leftMul]
+      change p * p⁻¹ = η[G]
+      exact (mul_inv_cancel p).trans (by
+        rw [CategoryTheory.Hom.one_def]
+        simp)
+    rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, ← Over.comp_left, h]
+    exact heU
+  have hFopen : ∀ W ∈ F, IsOpen W := by
+    intro W hW
+    obtain ⟨p, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hW
+    exact hVopen p
+  have hFnonempty : ∀ W ∈ F, W.Nonempty := by
+    intro W hW
+    obtain ⟨p, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hW
+    exact hVnonempty p
+  have hIrr := (isIrreducible_iff_sInter.mp
+    (IrreducibleSpace.isIrreducible_univ G.left)) F hFopen (by
+      intro W hW
+      simpa using hFnonempty W hW)
+  have hInter : (⋂₀ (↑F : Set (Set G.left))).Nonempty := by
+    simpa using hIrr
+  have hInterOpen : IsOpen (⋂₀ (↑F : Set (Set G.left))) :=
+    F.finite_toSet.isOpen_sInter hFopen
+  letI : JacobsonSpace G.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace G.hom
+  obtain ⟨g, hgF, hgc⟩ :=
+    nonempty_inter_closedPoints hInter hInterOpen.isLocallyClosed
+  let q0 := (pointEquivClosedPoint G.hom).symm ⟨g, hgc⟩
+  let q : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G := Over.homMk q0.1 q0.2
+  have hq : q.left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = g := by
+    dsimp [q, q0]
+    exact pointOfClosedPoint_apply G.hom g hgc (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)
+  refine ⟨⟨(rightMulIso G q).hom.left ⁻¹ᵁ A.1,
+    A.2.preimage (rightMulIso G q).hom.left⟩, ?_⟩
+  intro p hp
+  have hpF : V p ∈ F := Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩
+  have hgp : g ∈ V p := Set.mem_sInter.mp hgF _ hpF
+  change (rightMul G q).left (p.left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)) ∈ U
+  rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, ← Over.comp_left,
+    point_comp_rightMul_eq_point_comp_leftMul G p q,
+    Over.comp_left, Scheme.Hom.comp_apply, hq]
+  exact hgp
+
+/-- Every finite set of topological points of an irreducible locally algebraic
+group over an algebraically closed field lies in one affine open. -/
+theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAlgClosed_of_irreducible
+    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G] [IsAlgClosed K]
+    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [IrreducibleSpace G.left] :
+    Scheme.FiniteInAffine G.left := by
+  classical
+  intro s hs
+  lift s to Finset G.left using hs with t ht
+  letI : JacobsonSpace G.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace G.hom
+  have hclosed (x : G.left) :
+      ∃ y : G.left, y ∈ closure {x} ∧ y ∈ closedPoints G.left := by
+    have hnonempty : (closure ({x} : Set G.left)).Nonempty :=
+      ⟨x, subset_closure (Set.mem_singleton x)⟩
+    obtain ⟨y, hy, hyc⟩ :=
+      nonempty_inter_closedPoints hnonempty isClosed_closure.isLocallyClosed
+    exact ⟨y, hy, hyc⟩
+  choose y hy using hclosed
+  let p0 (x : G.left) := (pointEquivClosedPoint G.hom).symm ⟨y x, (hy x).2⟩
+  let p (x : G.left) : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ G :=
+    Over.homMk (p0 x).1 (p0 x).2
+  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ :=
+    exists_affineOpen_finset_points_of_irreducible G (t.image p)
+  refine ⟨A, ?_⟩
+  intro x hx
+  have hxt : x ∈ t := by
+    exact_mod_cast hx
+  have hp : p x ∈ t.image p := Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x, hxt, rfl⟩
+  have hpx : (p x).left (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = y x := by
+    dsimp [p, p0]
+    exact pointOfClosedPoint_apply G.hom (y x) (hy x).2
+      (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)
+  have hpy : y x ∈ A.1 := hpx ▸ hA (p x) hp
+  exact (specializes_iff_mem_closure.mpr (hy x).1).mem_open A.1.isOpen hpy
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme

Lemma 39.8.6. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $G$ be a locally algebraic group scheme over $k$. Let $g_1, \ldots , g_ n \in G(k)$ be $k$-rational points. Then there exists an affine open $U \subset G$ containing $g_1, \ldots , g_ n$.

Proof. We first argue by induction on $n$ that we may assume all $g_ i$ are on the same connected component of $G$. Namely, if not, then we can find a decomposition $G = W_1 \amalg W_2$ with $W_ i$ open in $G$ and (after possibly renumbering) $g_1, \ldots , g_ r \in W_1$ and $g_{r + 1}, \ldots , g_ n \in W_2$ for some $0 < r < n$. By induction we can find affine opens $U_1$ and $U_2$ of $G$ with $g_1, \ldots , g_ r \in U_1$ and $g_{r + 1}, \ldots , g_ n \in U_2$. Then

\[ g_1, \ldots , g_ n \in (U_1 \cap W_1) \cup (U_2 \cap W_2) \]

is a solution to the problem. Thus we may assume $g_1, \ldots , g_ n$ are all on the same connected component of $G$. Translating by $g_1^{-1}$ we may assume $g_1, \ldots , g_ n \in G^0$ where $G^0 \subset G$ is as in Proposition 39.7.11. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $U$ of $e$, in particular $U \cap G^0$ is nonempty. Since $G^0$ is irreducible we see that

\[ G^0 \cap (Ug_1^{-1} \cap \ldots \cap Ug_ n^{-1}) \]

is nonempty. Since $G \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(k)$ is locally of finite type, also $G^0 \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(k)$ is locally of finite type, hence any nonempty open has a $k$-rational point. Thus we can pick $g \in G^0(k)$ with $g \in Ug_ i^{-1}$ for all $i$. Then $g_ i \in g^{-1}U$ for all $i$ and $g^{-1}U$ is the affine open we were looking for. $\square$

## 39.7 Properties of group schemes over a field

In this section we collect some properties of group schemes over a field. In the case of group schemes which are (locally) algebraic over a field we can say a lot more, see Section 39.8.

Lemma 39.7.1. If $(G, m)$ is a group scheme over a field $k$, then the multiplication map $m : G \times _ k G \to G$ is open.

Proof. The multiplication map is isomorphic to the projection map $\text{pr}_0 : G \times _ k G \to G$ because the diagram

\[ \xymatrix{ G \times _ k G \ar[d]^ m \ar[rrr]_{(g, g') \mapsto (m(g, g'), g')} & & & G \times _ k G \ar[d]^{(g, g') \mapsto g} \\ G \ar[rrr]^{\text{id}} & & & G } \]

is commutative with isomorphisms as horizontal arrows. The projection is open by Morphisms, Lemma 29.24.4. $\square$

Lemma 39.7.2. If $(G, m)$ is a group scheme over a field $k$. Let $U \subset G$ open and $T \to G$ a morphism of schemes. Then the image of the composition $T \times _ k U \to G \times _ k G \to G$ is open.

Proof. For any field extension $K/k$ the morphism $G_ K \to G$ is open (Morphisms, Lemma 29.24.4). Every point $\xi $ of $T \times _ k U$ is the image of a morphism $(t, u) : \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K) \to T \times _ k U$ for some $K$. Then the image of $T_ K \times _ K U_ K = (T \times _ k U)_ K \to G_ K$ contains the translate $t \cdot U_ K$ which is open. Combining these facts we see that the image of $T \times _ k U \to G$ contains an open neighbourhood of the image of $\xi $. Since $\xi $ was arbitrary we win. $\square$

Proof. By definition a morphism of schemes $g : Y \to T$ is quasi-projective if it is locally of finite type, quasi-compact, and there exists a $g$-ample invertible sheaf on $Y$. Let $K/k$ be a field extension such that $X_ K$ is quasi-projective over $K$. Let $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A) \subset X$ be an affine open. Then $U_ K$ is an affine open subscheme of $X_ K$, hence $A_ K$ is a $K$-algebra of finite type. Then $A$ is a $k$-algebra of finite type by Algebra, Lemma 10.126.1. Hence $X \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(k)$ is locally of finite type. Since $X_ K \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(K)$ is quasi-compact, we see that $X_ K$ is quasi-compact, hence $X$ is quasi-compact, hence $X \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(k)$ is of finite type. By Morphisms, Lemma 29.40.4 we see that $X_ K$ has an ample invertible sheaf. Then $X$ has an ample invertible sheaf by Lemma 33.15.1. Hence $X \to \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(k)$ is quasi-projective by Morphisms, Lemma 29.40.4. $\square$

The group-scheme route is mathematically valid, but the exact arbitrary-field primitive is missing from Lean.

A conditional bridge already works:

```lean
letI : GrpObj P.gluedOver :=
  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy P.gluedOver
    (pic0Functor ((baseChange K P.N.1).obj C) ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) rep

exact Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine _
  (GroupScheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAlgClosed_of_irreducible P.gluedOver)
```

Relevant declarations:

- [`GroupScheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAlgClosed_of_irreducible`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/GroupAffineOpen.lean:162)
- Translation infrastructure `rightMulIso`, `leftMulIso`, and `point_comp_rightMul_eq_point_comp_leftMul` in [GroupAffineOpen.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/GroupAffineOpen.lean:37)
- Mathlib’s underlying [`GrpObj.mulRight`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.lake-packages/mathlib/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Grp.lean:275)
- The identical representability-to-group-object pattern in [`PicRepDatum.grpObj`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/PicRepDatum.lean:108)
- [`Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage.instLocallyOfFiniteTypeGluedMap`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteStageGeometry.lean:49)
- [`instQuasiCompactGluedMap`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteStageGeometry.lean:76)
- [`Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/FiniteInAffine.lean:66)

The conditional theorem cannot currently be applied because it requires:

```lean
[IsAlgClosed P.N.1]
[IrreducibleSpace P.glueData.glued]
```

Neither is available. `P.N.1` is the finite Galois descent field, not an algebraically closed field. No irreducibility theorem for the glued carrier exists either, although that part could plausibly follow later from a verified base-change identification. Per I-2004, the quarantined gluing-diagram draft cannot supply it.

The precise useful missing primitive is therefore:

```lean
theorem GroupScheme.finiteInAffine_of_finiteType
    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] :
    Scheme.FiniteInAffine G.left
```

This is the direct finite-in-affine consequence of the theorem that every algebraic group scheme over a field is quasi-projective. The mathematical result holds over arbitrary fields ([Stacks 39.8.7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BF7)), but Mathlib has no corresponding group-scheme quasi-projectivity or descent theorem at this pin.

The existing translation proof only handles rational points over an algebraically closed field. Its translations are indexed by sections `𝟙_ (Over (Spec k)) ⟶ G`, so they cannot directly translate arbitrary closed or nonclosed points over `P.N.1`.

Once the missing theorem exists, the exact orbit proof needs no projective-space immersion and no compatibility proof between the Galois action and multiplication: `FiniteInAffine` applies to every finite action through `orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine`.
